lessons.title: Reuse your product card
lessons.concept: A component is a reusable piece of interface. A prop gives it information. The same card can display a bag or a lamp.

explanation.text: Render two ProductCard components with different names. Change the component’s style once: both cards change.

exercise.task: The product is called Lampe. What value should name receive?
hints: A component is a reusable piece of interface. A prop gives it information. The same card can display a bag or a lamp.

quiz.question: The product is called Lampe. What value should name receive?
quiz.explanation: Nice! name receives Lampe, and {name} displays that value in the heading. Curly braces read a JavaScript value.
answerExplanations: Inside quotes, name is literal text: the card would show the word name. Pass the product’s name instead.
The component works, but would display Sac. Change only the prop to display Lampe.
Nice! name receives Lampe, and {name} displays that value in the heading. Curly braces read a JavaScript value.

lessons.title: Make your cart work
lessons.concept: State is a component’s memory. setCount asks React to remember a new quantity and update the display. A click handler needs a Client Component.

explanation.text: Create this component, import it into your page and click three times. Then add a button that resets the cart to zero.

exercise.task: The cart starts at 0. Complete the action to add 1 on each click.
hints: State is a component’s memory. setCount asks React to remember a new quantity and update the display. A click handler needs a Client Component.

quiz.question: The cart starts at 0. Complete the action to add 1 on each click.
quiz.explanation: Exactly! current is the previous quantity. Return that quantity plus 1. Try three clicks in the preview.
answerExplanations: Exactly! current is the previous quantity. Return that quantity plus 1. Try three clicks in the preview.
Every click sets the quantity to 1. After three clicks, it is still 1. Start from the previous quantity instead.
This calculation saves nothing. Without setCount, React receives no new value to display.

lessons.title: Put each job in the right place
lessons.concept: The server prepares data. The browser responds to clicks. Keep secrets on the server; add use client to components that need interaction.

explanation.text: Draw two columns: server and browser. Place product reads, private keys and cart clicks. Explain your choices before connecting Supabase.

exercise.task: Where should a private key with database administrator access live?
hints: The server prepares data. The browser responds to clicks. Keep secrets on the server; add use client to components that need interaction.

quiz.question: Where should a private key with database administrator access live?
quiz.explanation: Yes. server-only prevents importing this module into client code. Private operations must also check the user’s identity and permissions.
answerExplanations: NEXT_PUBLIC_ exposes a variable to the browser. An administrator key must remain private on the server.
Your button is a Client Component. Code sent to the browser can be inspected: do not give it a private key.
Yes. server-only prevents importing this module into client code. Private operations must also check the user’s identity and permissions.
